rapport_notes: Warm, attentive tone; good listening and clarification; professional demeanor throughout.
process_discipline_notes: No repeats detected; no silence violations (customer objection short-circuited the close sequence naturally).

evidence_quotes.agenda: are there any ches top of mind, important questions that I just wanna make sure that I answered today? — asked after Daniel had already volunteered that it's a small move with specific details.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No follow-up probing on the customer's stated concerns (or lack thereof). When Daniel said 'I don't think so. This is a pretty small move,' Chauntelle moved directly into logistics gathering without exploring whether there were hidden concerns.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: I'm actually getting this to about the two and a half to, let's just say three and a half hour mark. And so I have an hourly rate of $222 an hour — gives a time range but does not personalize it to access complexity (10 steps vs. 100-foot hallway), only lists general inclusions.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: we have a minimum of two and a half hours and so if you get closer to that two and a half to three hours, then that's all you'll pay for at the end of the day — states the beats-it-pay-less concept. Also: 'estimate is a window' framed as 'range of time' but not explained as tied to specific move factors. No commit-to-rate experience statement, no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' followed by silence (customer objected on price, rep pivoted to availability/hold instead).
evidence_quotes.close: No rate-lock mention. No explicit close ask — call ended with 'if you choose to move forward you could just reply to the email' (soft option, not a direct ask). Customer never booked.

top_strength: Chauntelle gathered inventory and access details with excellent clarity and patience, repeating back and confirming each element so nothing was missed for the estimate.
coaching_note: Critical: open every call with quid pro quo framing (time-boxed ask + quote promise) before probing, and ask 'other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' before diving into logistics—you asked the agenda line too late and never dug into the customer's real concerns, missing the opportunity to address them or set up Stage 2 takeaways.
